nonblocking_findings: F1 [Major] tests: The narrow mutant M3 (delete only the step 6 title suffix, both looks) passes the suite. The test asserts html.toContain('Past tense') (chibi-quest-step-names.test.ts line 131), which the Challenge line of template line 1812 satisfies, and tpl.toContain('{{#if grammar_search_term}}') (test line 137), which the same token satisfies. The sectionTitles helper strips the suffix (test line 82), so no assertion sees the rendered title with its grammar term. Rationale: This gap matters narrowly. A surgical regression would drop the grammar topic from the printed step 6 sign in every book, and no test would fail; the golden lesson has no grammar term, so the golden guard does not catch it either (M3 capture shows exit 0). The caught form M3b proves the whole-conditional deletion fails. Fix with one raw assertion: expect the classic render to contain 'Collect Sentences – Past tense' and the chibi render to contain 'Sentence Collection – Past tense'. The S5 page proofs cover the near-term print visually, so this does not block S4.

F2 [Nit] evidence: The Green evidence records 'git diff a4f52b9e -- dashboard/**/golden/**' as the golden-unchanged proof (plan.md line 100; green-s4-18d02125.log line 46). The golden files live under content/primary/origins-3.2/print/golden/, not under dashboard/, so that command is empty on every tree and proves nothing. Rationale: The claim itself holds. I ran git diff a4f52b9e..43dbf848 --stat -- dashboard/lib/teacher-manual/ content/primary/origins-3.2/print/golden/ and got 0 changed lines, and the golden byte-identity test passed in the gate. Record the correct path next time a phase cites this proof.

F3 [Nit] tests: The classic branch of the teacher-page heading has no test. No test renders wrapWorkbookDocument with look 'classic' or no look plus includeTeacherGuide and asserts 'Key Vocabulary' on the h4. A mutant that makes both branches of teacher-guide.ts line 14 read 'Preview Vocabulary' passes the suite. Rationale: The chibi direction is covered (test lines 177 to 178), and the flip mutant is caught, so the risk is a one-sided classic regression in the 5 printed books. One extra assertion closes it.
